Start with a published dataset when you need a citable version for analysis. Each repository record provides its own description, files, and citation information. Check the sampling dates and coverage in the files; a release date is not a sampling date.

## Published datasets

::: {.table-responsive role="region" aria-label="Published datasets" tabindex="0"}

| Dataset | Version or scope | Repository record |
|---|---|---|
| Database snapshot | Copy of the Shale Network database as of June 17, 2022 | [Penn State Data Commons](https://doi.org/10.26208/Z1HH-BX03) |
| Pennsylvania groundwater | September 2024 compilation used in the regional salinization study | [Penn State Data Commons](https://doi.org/10.26208/DT5Y-5B37) |
| Southwestern Pennsylvania groundwater | Beaver, Washington, and Greene counties; 2022 study dataset | [Penn State Data Commons](https://doi.org/10.26208/2NQE-WD53) |
| Bradford County groundwater | May 2018 compilation | [Penn State Data Commons](https://doi.org/10.26208/RJ0H-QF52) |
| Lycoming County groundwater | October 2018 compilation used in the Sugar Run study | [Penn State Data Commons](https://doi.org/10.18113/D35M2X) |
| Northeastern U.S. stream chemistry | Dataset accompanying the 2020 stream methane study | [Article and supplementary data](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2020.140105) |

:::

The June 2022 snapshot is a dated archive, not a representation of the database totals reported in October 2026. For a more recent extract or help selecting a dataset, contact [Tao Wen](mailto:twen08@syr.edu).

[Dataset highlights](data-highlights.qmd) explain the associated studies and their scope.

## Search across sites and measurements

[CUAHSI HydroClient](https://data.cuahsi.org/) is another route for discovering hydrologic observations. Use the [Shale Network database record](https://doi.org/10.4211/his-data-shalenetwork) to identify the collection. If a search or download is unavailable, use a published dataset above or contact the project team.

## Measurements represented

Available analytes differ among sites and datasets. Examples include:

- **General water chemistry:** pH, specific conductance, alkalinity, acidity, hardness, total dissolved solids, and suspended solids.
- **Major ions and nutrients:** sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, chloride, bromide, sulfate, ammonium, nitrate, and nitrite.
- **Trace constituents:** arsenic, barium, iron, manganese, lead, strontium, and other elements.
- **Gases, organic compounds, and radioactivity:** methane, selected organic compounds, gross alpha and beta measurements, and radium isotopes.

Consult the downloaded metadata for the exact variable name, units, analytical method, and reporting qualifiers. Read the [data-use guidance](data-use-and-embargo-policy.qmd) before reuse.
